_doc: Revert-verify mutants for #4482, PLUGIN half — the same core subject (`stripTemplateFrontmatter`) judged through the plugin's own surface (`extractTemplateBody` / `resolveTemplateForInsert`), because the plugin is a SECOND user-facing consumer with two distinct actions. Run from the repo root after replacing the path placeholders: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file>. Axis names are P<N>, the FIRST token of each test title, distinct from the core half's T<N>.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/services/TemplateBodyResolver.ts
_note_reach: The plugin jest config maps `^@kitelev/exocortex-core$` to `<rootDir>/../core/src/index.ts`, so this harness reaches the EDITED core source rather than a built `dist` — that is why a core-subject mutant can redden a plugin axis at all (harness-invocation-surface §A8). P4 is the LF/CRLF byte-parity control for the plugin surface and stays green under M1.

M1_restores_the_local_narrow_predicate._note: The pre-#4482 reach. P1/P2 show the template's own frontmatter leaking into the inserted body; P3 shows the editor path additionally RESOLVING a `$token` inside that leaked frontmatter line. P4 stays green — the LF and CRLF paths were never affected, which is why two plugin actions shipped this defect under a green suite. P5 stays GREEN under this mutant — its opening fence is LF-terminated, so the reintroduced `^---\r?\n` test passes and the block is still found; the mixed-EOL defect this axis guards is the SEPARATOR one, pinned by M6.

M2_drops_the_separating_terminator._note: Every inserted body would open with a blank line — the plugin surface is where a user SEES that immediately, so all four axes carry it. P5 reddens too: its body keeps the bare CR that followed the closing fence.

M3_narrows_the_separating_terminator_to_._note: Only an LF separator is consumed: the lone-CR axes (P1/P3) and the CRLF half of the control (P4) keep a leading terminator, while P2 — LF fences behind a BOM — stays green, which distinguishes this mutant from M1. P5 reddens: its separator is a bare CR, which an LF-only terminator cannot consume.

M4_reorders_separating_terminator_cr_bef._note: Plugin twin of the core M4 — only the CRLF half of the control (P4) can see a CR-first alternation; the lone-CR axes have nothing but a bare CR to give.

M5_separating_terminator_drops_the_bare_._note: Plugin twin of the core M5 — the lone-CR axes (P1/P3) and the mixed-EOL axis (P5) redden, P2 (LF fences behind a BOM) and the LF half of P4 stay green.

M6_separator_taken_from_the_OPENING_fenc._note: Plugin twin of the core M6 ('simplify for symmetry'): reddens ONLY P5, which is why that axis had to exist on this surface too.
